The image [0, heap-line) plus the mutable globals is the whole program
state; wasm call frames live engine-side, so one contiguous copy
re-enters the exact address space with every interior pointer valid.
The emitter projects three facts of a module over itself, emitted only
when the reachable tree performs an image op: $build_key hashes the fn
table names, the interned data, and the mutable-global census — the
three same-build-only word classes a restored image depends on;
$globals_save/$globals_restore walk that census at 8 bytes a slot with
the heap line at slot 0; $image_restore reads the wire's globals before
the copy and then swaps the image in with one memory.copy, whose
memmove semantics make the overlapping self-copy exact — the staging
buffer the first design carried deleted itself.

persist.mn sheds the record-copy prototype whole. persist(k, path)
drops the caller-supplied size; rehydrate refuses through two gates:
the build key, and the world fingerprint re-purposed — the restore runs
inside a perform's dynamic extent, every enclosing bracket writes back
a pre-swap world address as it unwinds, and the name-level fingerprint
is the install-prefix correspondence that makes those addresses valid
in the restored image. E_ResumeWorldMismatchWorld had zero raise sites
and dies; the refusal rides fail with both worlds named.

Gate: run_persist_image, one build and two processes — leg A persists
mid-computation (40), leg B re-enters the image, reads the typed root
through the restored globals record, and runs A's thunk against A's
heap pointees (42); corrupted key and corrupted fingerprint both refuse
with teaching messages. Red on the pre-image boot: the substrate ops
are unrecognized and the executable refuses at compile.

mentl/f88bb51:
An arm that never resumes but returns a meaningful value must deliver that
value as the install's, abandoning the continuation. This is a distinct
resume discipline, not a MultiShot special case: abandon has no live
continuation, so it lowers differently from a resume, and the op scheme has
to carry which. Abandon joins OneShot, MultiShot, and Either.

The classifier gates the flip on the op's return type. A UZero grade over a
bare quantified type variable (fail's polymorphic bottom) or the never type
is bottom, with no value to abandon, so it stays OneShot. Only a concrete
non-unit return flips to Abandon. The wheel's own abort returns the never
type and fail returns a bare variable, so no wheel op changes discipline and
the wheel compiles the same set of nodes; the m2/m3 difference is purely the
k-machinery emit change crossing one generation.

The mechanism: an Abandon perform yields with a dead k, and the emit floors
on the empty op name rather than the k value so an abandon yield's bare-const
k takes the real yield path. An Abandon perform diverges, so the block
lowering truncates at the first diverging statement, and post-abort effectful
code cannot run. The driver counts Abandon ops and delivers the arm value on
flag-clear, which is abandon by construction. The k2 boundary descends into a
constructor call's arguments and rebuilds the variant with the boundary
replaced by the hole, so the Some(risky()) shape reifies; a fn-call remainder
stays unbuilt and loud. A resume whose continuation aborts yields a foreign
op back through the redrive, which now propagates it to the enclosing driver
instead of flooring. And an install whose body directly yields an op its
driver does not cover is no longer treated as guarded, so an abandon-armed
handler does not silently defeat the driverless-crossing floor.

mentl/f87abf3:
Mentl IS speculative inference. Per Q-Morgan-A: she uses inference's
primitives (graph_bind via trail-rollback) to explore alternate
realities at every position with active dependents. She is not a peer
to inference — she is inference run forward with hypothetical
bindings rolled back, the survivors recorded as candidates.

The oracle's exploration is Pure over (env + handler_chain + intent),
matching IC's existing Pure over (ast + imports + handler_chain +
intent). Per the IC + oracle composition (Q-Morgan-IC): IC's Cache
handler stores (env, oracle_queue) per module instead of just env.
Same invalidation discipline; same Pure-enables-memoization principle;
the oracle's continuous-subscription substrate falls out of IC for
free. ONE change to the cache key. ONE additional cached value. The
rest falls out.

Per Q-Morgan-B (silence-only-at-gradient-top): the project queue is a
sorted merge of per-module cached queues. Surfaces query via
OracleQuery; surface query is itself memoizable (Pure over the set of
cache hashes). Mentl is silent ONLY when the project queue is empty —
the gradient's top, the proven-complete state. Until then Mentl
always surfaces the highest-priority next step.

The build IS a `<~` feedback loop (per INSIGHTS L1761): source change
→ IC invalidates affected modules → re-infer + re-explore → project
queue refreshes → highest-priority next-step surfaces → user acts →
loop. This isn't a hidden runtime daemon — it's a visible feedback
topology where each loop iteration is bounded by IC's invalidation
work.
